newsitem.title: GERMANY: Hypo-Bank won't rule out capital increase.
newsitem.headline: Hypo-Bank won't rule out capital increase.

text.p: Bayerische Hypotheken- und Wechselbank AG reiterated on Tuesday it could not rule out a capital increase in 1997 or 1998 but added that it had not made concrete plans yet.
"We have not planned one but the possibility cannot be ruled out," chief executive Eberhard Martini told the bank's annual shareholder meeting.
Martini was reiterating comments he made at the bank's annual news conference in April.

He said at the time that the increase of Hypo-Bank's stake in British fund manager Foreign & Colonial last year to 65 percent from 50 percent and a strong expansion in mortgage lending in the final months of 1996 had affected its capital adequacy.
Hypo-Bank's core capital ratio fell to 4.9 percent in 1996 and its overall capital ratio fell to 8.5 percent from 9.1 percent in 1995.
The bank plans to issue profit participation certificates or warrant bonds this year to help beef up reserves.
